bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` file is empty, and the authoritative MemorySanitizer trace shows the crash occurs during `LLVMFuzzerInitialize` before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` consumes any testcase bytes. `LLVMFuzzerInitialize` calls `Py_InitializeFromConfig`, CPython imports frozen importlib code, and `PyEval_EvalCode` asks `_PyFunction_FromConstructor()` to build a temporary function object for that module execution. `_PyFunction_FromConstructor` allocates a fresh `PyFunctionObject` with `PyObject_GC_New`, which ultimately comes from `malloc` and does not zero the function payload. The constructor then initializes many pointer fields and `vectorcall`, but it never writes `func_version` before calling `_PyFunction_SetVersion(op, 0)`. The generic setter first checks `if (func->func_version != 0)` to invalidate the previous cache slot, so on this fresh object it branches on the still-indeterminate heap contents of `func_version`, producing the saved MSan `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `Objects/funcobject.c:272`. The staged trace later records the same stale-field read from `PyFunction_NewWithQualName`, and the fix changes both fresh-object constructors to write `func_version = 0` directly instead of routing through `_PyFunction_SetVersion`.

source.description: First source-grounded materialization of the poisoned state on the witnessed startup chain. `_PyFunction_FromConstructor()` allocates a fresh `PyFunctionObject`, and the saved MSan origin stack points to this allocation as the creation point of the bytes later read from `func_version`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` file is zero bytes and no testcase payload is consumed. The authoritative trace fires during `LLVMFuzzerInitialize -> Py_InitializeFromConfig -> PyEval_EvalCode`, which reaches this allocation while importing frozen importlib code.

root_cause.description: Missing initialization obligation on the fresh-object constructor path. `_PyFunction_FromConstructor()` calls the generic version setter before any write has defined `op->func_version`.
root_cause.note: The preceding constructor assignments populate globals, builtins, name, qualname, code, defaults, doc, module, annotations, typeparams, and `vectorcall`, but not `func_version`. The patch fixes this exact obligation by replacing the setter call with `op->func_version = 0;`; it makes the same change in `PyFunction_NewWithQualName()` because the staged trace shows the same bug pattern there too.

sink.description: MSan crash site. `_PyFunction_SetVersion()` reads the previous `func_version` to invalidate the version-cache slot, but on the fresh constructor path that field still holds uninitialized heap data.
sink.note: The saved default trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `Objects/funcobject.c:272:9` with stack `_PyFunction_SetVersion -> _PyFunction_FromConstructor -> PyEval_EvalCode -> exec_code_in_module`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan origin. The uninitialized `func_version` bytes later read at the sink originate in the fresh `PyFunctionObject` heap allocation.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved origin stack is `_PyObject_GC_New -> _PyFunction_FromConstructor -> PyEval_EvalCode -> exec_code_in_module -> PyImport_ImportFrozenModuleObject -> Py_InitializeFromConfig -> LLVMFuzzerInitialize`.

coarse_trace.summary: Harness initialization calls `Py_InitializeFromConfig()`. The authoritative staged MSan report fires on this startup path before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` consumes any testcase bytes.
During frozen importlib startup, `PyEval_EvalCode()` wraps a module code object in a temporary function by calling `_PyFunction_FromConstructor()`.
The constructor allocates a fresh `PyFunctionObject`, initializes many members but not `func_version`, and then calls `_PyFunction_SetVersion(op, 0)`.
The generic version setter reads `func->func_version` to evict any old cache entry; on this fresh object that branch consumes uninitialized heap data and MSan reports the read.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact staged `poc` is zero bytes, but the authoritative trace shows the crash happens during interpreter startup before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` runs. `LLVMFuzzerInitialize()` calls `Py_InitializeFromConfig()`, which imports frozen modules and reaches the later function-constructor path.

While executing frozen importlib code during startup, `PyEval_EvalCode()` asks `_PyFunction_FromConstructor()` to build the temporary function object used to evaluate that module. This selects the `_PyFunction_FromConstructor` path from the first saved MSan stack.

Source and MSan origin. `PyObject_GC_New()` allocates a fresh GC-tracked function object. `_PyObject_GC_New()` only initializes the GC/header words, so the payload field `func_version` is still indeterminate until this constructor writes it.

Root cause. This constructor reaches the generic setter on a brand-new object even though the earlier assignments in lines 119-133 never wrote `func_version`. The setter therefore receives `op` while its previous-version field is still the uninitialized heap state from step 3.

Sink. `_PyFunction_SetVersion()` first checks the old `func_version` to invalidate any cached slot before storing the new version. On this fresh-object path that branch reads the still-uninitialized field and produces the saved MemorySanitizer report.

allocation_context.description: The saved origin stack points to the fresh `PyFunctionObject` allocation at this constructor line; that object's `func_version` field is not initialized before the later setter-side read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSan's origin is the fresh `PyFunctionObject` allocation at `_PyFunction_FromConstructor:114`, and the root cause is the immediate call to `_PyFunction_SetVersion(op, 0)` before any write defines `op->func_version`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The fine trace follows the first authoritative stack `_PyFunction_SetVersion -> _PyFunction_FromConstructor -> PyEval_EvalCode -> exec_code_in_module -> Py_InitializeFromConfig -> LLVMFuzzerInitialize`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The same `func_version` bytes created at the fresh allocation remain unwritten through the constructor and are read by `_PyFunction_SetVersion`'s `if (func->func_version != 0)` guard. The crash happens before any testcase bytes are consumed.

poc.trigger: The exact staged witness is the zero-byte file `poc`. On the authoritative run the crash occurs in `LLVMFuzzerInitialize`, during `Py_InitializeFromConfig` startup import, before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` consumes any testcase bytes.

format.contract: Use the exact staged zero-byte `poc`. The verified trigger semantics do not rely on any testcase bytes: the saved MemorySanitizer trace fires during `LLVMFuzzerInitialize -> Py_InitializeFromConfig` while CPython imports frozen importlib code, before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` reads the file contents. This Stage 02 contract therefore stays at the exact empty witness and the observed startup path; it does not generalize to other input lengths or claim testcase-byte influence on the crash.
